native/angr-macros is a workspace crate (proc-macro2/quote/syn) added to close the "same invariant, upheld at some call sites but not others" bug family from the angr-9ke6b/angr-sqfj8 audits (~45% of bugs in both rounds shared this shape). Three macros:

- #[angr_macros::steady_guarded] (attribute macro): injects `self.steady_config_guard();` as the method first statement. Applied uniformly across all RustExplorationManager mutators in manager_methods*.rs, replacing hand-written calls so a new mutator cannot forget it (closed angr-sqfj8.28/.29). Two documented exceptions, both because the guard must NOT be the unconditional first statement: load_snapshot_bytes (guard must run after a fallible parse) and set_parallel_frontier_residency. Both now carry #[angr_macros::steady_guard_exempt(reason = "...")] instead of the old doc-comment convention (see steady_guard_checked below).
- #[derive(angr_macros::MergePolicy)] (derive macro): requires every field of the annotated struct (RustSimState) to carry #[merge_policy = "..."] naming one of self_wins/computed/delegate/union/max/min/warn_on_diverge/joint. Adding a field without one is a compile error.
  Since angr-12jjk.9 it ALSO GENERATES the merge expression for the five mechanical policies (MECHANICAL_MERGE_POLICIES = self_wins/union/max/min/warn_on_diverge) as a private `merge_field_<name>(&self, others: &[&Self]) -> FieldTy`, which state/fork.rs::RustSimState::merge must call. Enforcement is dead_code: a generated method merge never calls is an unused private method, which CI clippy -D warnings rejects — so the label and the merge line cannot drift apart. delegate/computed/joint stay hand-written (whole-slice or cross-field logic: fs longest-stdout scan, hooks reading removed_hooks). A mechanical field whose type does not fit the generated body opts out with #[merge_manual = "<why>"] (non-empty reason required; using it on a non-mechanical policy is a compile error). Derive-site requirement: warn_config_divergence(&str, bool) must be in scope where the struct is defined.
- #[angr_macros::steady_guard_checked] (attribute macro, applied to the impl block, not the fn): closes the opt-in gap steady_guarded left open — see KEY ASYMMETRY below, now RESOLVED.

THIRD ENFORCEMENT MECHANISM, no macro needed (angr-91vj9.1): make the unchecked value UNREPRESENTABLE. syscalls::mod's `BoundedArg { Within(u64), Exceeds }` — returned by `extract_bounded_concrete_arg` (raw arg + cap in one call) and `bounded_value` (derived quantity, e.g. brk's growth, or a length old_mmap read out of a guest struct) — puts the guest-controlled size behind a match, so a new bounded call site does not compile until its author writes the refusal arm. That is strictly stronger than the extract-then-`if v > max` shape the round-3 findings kept forgetting, and it needs no proc-macro and no coverage script. Reach for this first when the invariant is "this value must not be used before check X"; reach for an attribute macro only when the invariant is a *statement* to inject rather than a value to gate. The same pattern closed SP/return-address default-to-zero too: AddrOrSymbolic (arch/mod.rs) wraps VEXInterpreter::get_stack_pointer / get_return_addr and RustExplorationManager::get_return_addr's Option<u64> return, with no Default/From<u64> impl, so a bare .unwrap_or(0) on the value no longer compiles — tools/audit_sp_default_zero.py stays as a backstop only for the generic get_offset_u64/get_sp_value accessors it deliberately left untyped, and for the .concrete() escape hatch a caller could still misuse. FIFTH/SIXTH/SEVENTH MACROS, function-like (angr-0jh0j.6, angr-6cp06.79): callback_setters!, inspect_test_entries! and inspect_dispatch!, all over callbacks/ (callback_setters! in callbacks/mod.rs; the inspect_test_entries! invocation moved to callbacks/inspect_test_entries.rs in angr-5mnx3.8). HARD CONSTRAINT they establish for any future PyO3-surface generator: an attribute proc macro expands OUTER-FIRST, so #[pymethods] on a hand-written impl block cannot see through an unexpanded macro_rules!/proc-macro invocation sitting inside it — the generated fns are invisible to PyO3 and never reach Python. A generator of #[pymethods] items must therefore live at MODULE level and emit its own `#[pymethods] impl Type { .. }` block (fine here: the multiple-pymethods feature is already on for the manager_methods*.rs split). That is why both macros take the type name as an argument. Second constraint: macro_rules! cannot concatenate idents (no `paste` in the vendored registry, and no network), so anything deriving `set_<field>` / `py_call_inspect_<event>` from a list has to be a proc macro in angr-macros — reach there rather than hand-listing name pairs, which reintroduces the drift. Shapes worth copying: callback_setters! is driven from the existing with_callback_fields! list (its arm now passes any tokens before the field list through, so one list can feed consumers that need extra arguments); inspect_test_entries! takes ordinary `fn <event>(..) { .. self.forward(..) }` entries and rewrites the `forward` placeholder to `call_inspect_<event>`, rejecting a body that never calls it or that names a call_inspect_* method directly — a placeholder rewrite keeps arbitrary body code (the constraints entry imports its guard AST first) while still deriving the target, which a signature-DSL macro could not. Raw idents: `r#return` stringifies WITH its `r#` prefix, so strip it before format_ident! or the derived name is `call_inspect_r#return`.

SEVENTH MACRO detail (angr-6cp06.79): inspect_dispatch!, invoked in callbacks/inspect.rs, generates the call_inspect_<event> dispatch methods themselves — the layer BETWEEN the setters callback_setters! derives and the test entry points inspect_test_entries! derives, and the one where the hand-copied body could still read the sibling's slot (self.inspect_reg_read in call_inspect_reg_write typechecks). Same placeholder-rewrite shape, one step further: the placeholder self.with_slot(absent, f) expands to self.with_inspect_cb(self.inspect_<event>.as_ref(), absent, f), so the macro does not merely rewrite an ident, it INJECTS the derived field as a leading argument — recognize a placeholder ident only when a parenthesized group follows it, and prepend into that group. Both macros' parse form is now the shared EventFnEntries (Type => fn <event>(..) {..} ...). Rejects a body that never calls the placeholder, or that names with_inspect_cb / any inspect_* ident directly. Unlike its two siblings its expansion is a plain inherent impl (no #[pymethods]), so it CAN have tests/ui/ trybuild cases — it has three, one per diagnostic; the accumulate-don't-return pair is still asserted by count_compile_errors in inspect_dispatch_tests, which a single-error snapshot cannot show. The hand-written impl in inspect.rs keeps only what is not per-event: with_inspect_cb, inspect_event_enabled/inspect_bit_enabled, fire_constraints_bp.
angr-syscall-mips-o32-table-divergence: angr's MIPS-O32 syscall number table in angr/procedures/definitions/linux_kernel.py uses NUMBERS THAT DIFFER from upstream Linux for the *at family. Examples: mkdirat=4289 (upstream 4287), unlinkat=4294 (upstream 4292), renameat=4295 (upstream 4293), readlinkat=4298 (matches upstream), faccessat=4300 (matches upstream). Some match, some are off by +2. Why this matters: native Rust syscall handlers MUST use angr's numbers, not upstream Linux, because angr's SimSyscallLibrary maps syscall names -> numbers via this table, and our dispatcher receives the angr-issued number when a name-based syscall fires. Using upstream numbers would silently de-register the handler for that name. COROLLARY (angr-0jh0j.58): the same table also decides whether a syscall is registerable AT ALL on an arch -- getrandom exists in real Linux on ARM/AArch64/MIPS but has no entry in angr's arm/armhf/aarch64/mips-o32/mips-n64 maps, so NativeGetrandomSyscall is registered only for AMD64 (318) and X86 (355). Before adding a handler row for a new arch, confirm the name is in that arch's dict; 'the Linux ABI has it' is not sufficient. Awk to inspect by arch index: awk '/lib.add_number_mapping_from_dict/{c++} c==N && /<name>/' angr/procedures/definitions/linux_kernel.py where N=1 (aarch64), 2 (amd64), 3 (arm), 4 (armhf), 5 (i386), 6 (mips-n32), 7 (mips-n64), 8 (mips-o32).

arch-arm64-guest-state-tail: arm64 guest-state tail layout (fixed 2026-07-22, angr-a4xix + angr-zxzi3): VexGuestARM64State's guest_QCFLAG is a **U128** at 832, not a UInt. The tail therefore runs qcflag(832,16) emnote(848,4) cmstart(856,8) cmlen(864,8) nraddr(872,8) ip_at_syscall(880,8) fpcr(888,4), then 4 pad bytes and the LL/SC fallback block (896..928). native/angr/src/arch/arm64.rs::offsets previously had FPCR=836 -- INSIDE qcflag's own extent -- and GUEST_STATE_SIZE=848, which sized RegisterFile's buffer below ip_at_syscall/fpcr so IR PUTs there were silently dropped by RegisterFile::put's 'end <= data.len()' guard and GETs returned zero via the symmetric guard in RegisterFile::get. GUEST_STATE_SIZE is now 928: it must cover the unnamed LL/SC tail, not just the last NAMED register, or those PUTs vanish. LESSON: for any arch table, cross-check against /usr/include/valgrind/libvex_guest_<arch>.h (installed on this box) AND archinfo -- archinfo stops at the last register it models (fpcr for AArch64) so it under-reports the true guest-state size. A 16-byte register works end-to-end unchanged: RegisterFile::get/put are u128-based and RustBV::concrete(v,128) is fine. bounce-reduction-low-roi-corpus:
Bounce-reduction ('stay in Rust more') has LOW ROI on the real corpus (measured 2026-07-01 from baseline_counters.json, 32 benches). Of 4584 total Rust->Python callbacks: 3921 (86%) are lift_block (pyvex VEX lifting — INHERENT, Rust cannot lift VEX; warm cache already kills repeats). 201 are SimProcedure fallbacks but 130 of those are fseek(86)+fprintf(44) in ONE bench (sharif7_rev50) declining on SYMBOLIC args (native handlers exist in fileops.rs/stream_ops.rs but declare args=[...concrete] so symbolic offset/format falls back — needs symbolic file positions, a large FileSystem project, not a quick win); ~40 are USER Python hooks (my_scanf/get_flag/UserHook — irreducible per rust-python-boundary-audit); only ~20 corpus-wide are cleanly reducible (C++ operator new/delete->malloc/free mapping, a few memmove/strncpy symbolic-decline extensions). posix(452ms,31 benches) is a stateful Python plugin; CADET symbolic_branch/vex_fallback are hard. CONCLUSION: the engine already stays in Rust for ~everything reducible (99.997% block exec in Rust); remaining bounces are inherent (pyvex) or irreducible (user code, symbolic ops). The higher-value lever is making the PARALLEL path robust to unavoidable bounces (angr-nkoct: a >26x super-linear cliff detonates at ~96 bounces across a wide frontier at workers=4, despite modest reattaches + sub-ms GIL) rather than reducing bounce frequency. Companion bead angr-0xyq2 (native SimFile reads) is also narrow on this corpus (read appears once).

SCOPE LIMIT (added iter143 — read before using this to kill work): 'low ROI' here means AGGREGATE WALL TIME. It does NOT apply to the ZeroPy gate (gil_work_time_ns == 0), which is a COUNT predicate: 7 corpus benches are bounce-SOLE and 4 of them bounce a SimProcedure exactly ONCE, so retiring a single proc's fallback flips a whole bench to PASS. The part of this memory that DOES still bind the gate work is the taxonomy: symbolic-arg declines (bucket B) are fundable-but-sized, and USER Python hooks are IRREDUCIBLE (bucket C) — a bucket-C bench can never reach gil==0 and must leave the gate denominator instead. See invariant-zeropy-gate-levers-are-count-not-ns; beads angr-gorvf.12 (classify) / .13 (impl).
callbacks-unit-test-harness: PythonCallbacks unit-test harness (angr-9ke6b.28): native/angr/src/callbacks/{dispatch_tests.rs,inspect_tests.rs} share a 3-fn helper trio that since angr-5mnx3.7 lives in ONE place — callbacks/test_support.rs, wired from mod.rs with test_submod!(test_support) and imported by both via 'use crate::callbacks::test_support::{defs, obj, recorder}'. It sits a level ABOVE both consumers (dispatch_tests is a child of dispatch, inspect_tests of inspect), so the helpers are pub(super) = visible throughout the callbacks subtree; add new shared callbacks test plumbing there rather than re-copying it. The trio: defs(py, c"...") runs a snippet in a fresh PyDict globals and returns it, obj(globals, name) pulls a callable out as Py<PyAny> for a set_* setter, recorder(globals, name) casts a snippet-defined list back for assertions. Precedent for the shape is vex/ops/test_helpers.rs. Two facts make these tests cheap and claripy-free: (1) every dispatch/inspect call_* checks its Option<Py<PyAny>> field BEFORE any py.import("claripy") or rustbv_to_claripy, so unset-arm tests need only Python::initialize(); (2) the test module is a descendant of mod callbacks, so private PythonCallbacks fields and private free fns (bv_to_bytes) are reachable via 'use super::*'. Wire a per-file test module with the test_submod! macro (crate::test_submod, defined in lib.rs, textual scope so no import) appended to the parent .rs: test_submod!("X_tests.rs" => X_tests); — NOT a hand-written #[cfg(test)] #[path=...] mod, which the macro exists to replace (it also carries the clippy::unwrap_used/expect_used opt-out test code needs). Since angr-0jh0j.7 every file in callbacks/ (mod.rs, config.rs, dispatch.rs, inspect.rs, inspect_bits.rs, events.rs) uses it uniformly. Note the two modules have OPPOSITE unset contracts: dispatch call_* must hard-error (avoid-silent-no-op-callback-fallbacks), inspect call_inspect_* must return Ok (no BP registered is normal). Testing a *wired* claripy-touching path (angr-0jh0j.5): the cargo-test interpreter has no claripy, so py.import("claripy") errors out before the code under test — take the module as a &Bound<PyAny> parameter (PythonCallbacks::fire_constraints_bp, split out of call_inspect_constraints) and pass a stub object defined by a defs() snippet. A stub whose BVV raises drives the export into failure; pair it with an exporting stub as a positive control so the failure assertion cannot pass vacuously. Prefer this over overwriting sys.modules["claripy"], which leaks across the shared cargo-test interpreter (the networkx stub in automaton/python_bindings_tests.rs is only safe because nothing else imports it).

cascmp-string-path-gap-root-cause: Iop_CasCmpEQ/CasCmpNE 8/16/32/64 were missing from the STRING path of opcode_map.rs::parse_comparison despite being correctly mapped in parse_opcode_from_u32 (0x1431-0x1438, comment 'same as CmpEQ/CmpNE'). pyvex's string-based lifting (which the angr Rust engine uses) silently dropped them via the IROp::Raw(0) fallback, causing cmpxchg/cmpxchg16b blocks to produce fresh-symbolic zeros that test_dcas_cmpxchg16b_no_match_keeps_memory was just-barely tolerating. This regression only surfaced when angr-tkbr.2 (commit 8b9ff2713) replaced the silent Raw(0) path with a hard typed error. Fix: add tuple_arms! mappings for CasCmpEQ/CasCmpNE in parse_comparison so they route to IROp::CmpEQ/CmpNE. Other ops likely have similar string-vs-integer-path gaps; when adding to parse_opcode_from_u32, mirror in parse_*. ADDENDUM (2026-08-03, iter163): parse_opcode_from_u32 and the whole numeric/FFI opcode path NO LONGER EXIST -- opcode_map.rs is string-only now (entry point parse_opcode, dispatching to parse_arithmetic/bitwise/shift/comparison/conversion/float/vector/vreverse/special/neon_unimplemented). Unmapped names now log::warn! and return IROp::Unmapped(intern_unmapped_op(op_str)), which dispatch turns into a typed UnsupportedVexOp error (no silent Raw(0)). So the 'mirror the numeric path' advice is moot; the live analogue is that a family can still be PARTIALLY mapped. Related invariant: the tuple_arms!/vec_arms!/scalar_arms! macros match the suffix EXACTLY (strip_prefix + literal match arm), so a suffixed sibling like Iop_ClzNat32 can never be silently mistaken for Iop_Clz32 -- it falls through to Unmapped and defers loudly. Known deliberate family gaps carry an 'unmapped for now'-style comment: Iop_CmpORD* in parse_comparison, and Iop_ClzNat/CtzNat in the parse_conversion catch-all arm (absent from vendor/pyvex_ffi.h on the current VEX pin; map them when the pin is bumped).
ccall-inc-dec-carry-preserve: Rust ccall rflags_c/eflags_c symbolic-carry path (handle_x86_eflags_c in native/angr/src/vex/ccall/mod.rs, reached from handle_ccall_with_ctx's name dispatch — it was inline in handle_ccall_with_ctx before the angr-5mnx3.60 helper split) must cover ALL OpCategory variants, not just Copy/Sub/Add/Logic. INC/DEC do NOT modify CF — VEX preserves it in cc_ndep (args[3]); the carry is CF=(cc_ndep>>G_CC_SHIFT_C)&1 (SHIFT_C==0), same formula as concrete calc_flags_inc/calc_flags_dec. angr-g6dg root cause: the rflags_c symbolic match had Inc/Dec in the '_ => None' arm, so when cc_dep1/cc_ndep were symbolic (cold blank_state blob, dec preserving carry) the whole ccall returned None and eval_ccall (expressions_arith.rs) substituted a FRESH unconstrained symbolic carry, poisoning flags threaded into later loop iterations. NOTE: a jnz/jz loop guard is often compiled by VEX to a direct CmpEQ32(result,0) (NO condition ccall), so a ZF-based countdown loop does NOT exercise this bug — you need a CF-dependent path (jc/jb/jae) or the carry-preservation chain through consecutive dec/inc. Fixed commit f761d0493 (Inc|Dec arms added). When adding cc_op categories, mirror both the concrete calc_flags_* and the symbolic SymFlags builder.
claripy-ast-hash-stability: claripy AST __hash__ is content-addressed and STABLE for a given AST object across CPython gc (verified empirically: hash(x) unchanged after gc.collect()). This is why claripy_bridge::cache's AST_CACHE is keyed by ast.hash() rather than id(ast), which CPython can recycle after collection. Two DISTINCT ASTs denoting the same symbol legitimately hash differently (annotations, BVS explicit_name suffixes) — that is what symbolic::registry::update_hash_mapping exists for, not hash mutation. A former claripy_bridge::get_stable_ast_id helper documented the opposite ('hash changes due to garbage collection or object reallocation') and preferred ast._hash over __hash__(); it was deleted in caf870723 (angr-9ke6b.214). Note ast._hash != hash(ast) in claripy 9.2.209, so resurrecting that preference would silently desync from the AST_CACHE key. Cross-cache invariant C5's width check lives in the AST_CACHE hit arm of claripy_bridge::import::claripy_to_rustbv_depth.

claripy-import-binary-op-helper: claripy_bridge/import.rs binary-op dispatch is DRY'd through import_binary_op() (angr-9ke6b.45): 24 arms (__add__/__sub__/__mul__/SDiv/__floordiv__|UDiv/SMod/__mod__|URem/__and__/__or__/__xor__/__lshift__/LShR/__rshift__/RotateLeft/RotateRight/__eq__/__ne__/ULT/ULE/UGT/UGE/SLT/SLE/SGT/SGE) are one-liners passing an arity-error label plus a 'fn(&RustBV,&RustBV,&SymContext)->RustBV' pointer. SCOPE LIMIT (angr-sqfj8.92): class (1)'s 'already caught elsewhere' rationale only holds for checks whose violation reaches the Python boundary or Z3. A precondition on a path that folds CONCRETELY (RustBV::reverse_owned's byte-alignment check was the found instance) never reaches either, so the blanket 'do NOT re-promote' does not cover it — such a site needs the invalid input actually HANDLED (reverse_owned now returns the operand unchanged for a non-byte-aligned width, matching value_z3.rs's own misaligned BVOp::Reverse arm), not asserted, since a dev-only panic against a release-only wrong answer is itself a profile divergence. When auditing a debug_assert! in these modules, ask first whether the guarded path can fold concretely. MISSED-BY-THE-SWEEP (angr-sqfj8.109): the .220 sweep was not exhaustive — syscalls/mprotect.rs NativeMprotectSyscall::call's set_page_permissions check appeared in neither list. Its fix is the third shape, distinct from both promote-to-assert! and handle-silently: the caller already HAS an error channel (mprotect returns -1 for an unmapped page), so the guard log::warn!s and returns that same -1 in every profile. Prefer this shape whenever the enclosing function can already report failure — assert! in release is a process abort (panic="abort"), so reserve it for invariants with no such channel. Absence from the .220 lists means 'unaudited', not 'deliberately kept'. SECOND SCOPE LIMIT (angr-0jh0j.72): class (1)'s 'already rejected at the Python boundary by symbolic/table.rs's binary-op macro' rationale only covers the ~25 ops routed through op_binary!. dfa-minimize-index-worklist-invariant: DFA::minimize (native/angr/src/automaton/dfa.rs) uses a NON-textbook Hopcroft worklist: entries are (partition_INDEX, symbol), not (partition_set, symbol). On a split the LARGER half keeps the old index -- silently inheriting every still-pending entry that named it -- and only the smaller half is enqueued under a fresh index. Soundness argument (an in-code comment above the worklist decl): determinism means a state has at most one s-successor, so pred(keep,s) and pred(add,s) are DISJOINT and their union is pred(Y,s); the inherited entry plus the fresh one together separate every pair the original splitter would have. That index invariant is now enforced by a debug_assert! at the dequeue site (angr-9ke6b.182 replaced an unreachable 'else { continue }' that would have silently dropped a splitter). NOTE: debug_assert! is compiled OUT of 'cargo test --release', which is what the ralph gate runs -- to actually exercise it use 'cargo test --manifest-path native/angr/Cargo.toml --lib automaton' (debug profile). NOT textbook Hopcroft and NO O(n*|Sigma|*log n) bound (angr-9ke6b.184): both initial partitions are seeded (not only the smaller), there is no in-worklist membership tracking, and each popped splitter rescans EVERY partition instead of only pred-touched ones; docs now say 'Hopcroft-style partition refinement' everywhere. Regression coverage in dfa_tests.rs: test_minimize_splits_pending_splitter (hand-traced 7-state case where 1 and 2 are told apart only by the inherited entry) and test_minimize_matches_moore_reference (400 LCG-seeded complete 2-symbol DFAs vs an independent table-filling reference, comparing class count AND language). TRAP found while writing these: minimize() does NOT return the empty DFA for a language-empty input that still has reachable states -- it returns the single non-final class (1 state), which is what Moore reports too; only start_state=None / num_states=0 / no reachable states take the DFA::new() early return. docs-citation-audit-method:
Docs file-path citations drift across refactors just like bd-memory citations. TWO distinct failure modes, and the cheap check only catches the first:
(1) Path no longer exists — audit with: grep -rhoE '(native/angr/src|angr/exploration)[A-Za-z0-9_/.]+\.(rs|py)' docs/ | sort -u | while read f; do [ -e "$f" ] || echo MISSING: $f; done. Found+repaired 3 stale vex/ir.rs refs in rust_vex_ops.rst (file split into vex/ir/ in zel8z.7) in commit f766f6e7b. Caveat: a MISSING hit can be intentional (rust_engine.rst cites deleted spike lineage_assumptions.rs with its recovery commit) — verify context before editing.
(2) Path still exists but the SYMBOL moved out of it — invisible to (1) and to check_line_citations.py. This is the dominant mode around exploration/mod.rs, which repeated splits (manager_methods_* pymethods split angr-nbim4.1, event.rs/callback_types.rs extraction angr-zel8z.3) hollowed into a wiring module while docs kept citing it. Audit by resolving the SYMBOL, not the file: for each 'file.rs::sym' or 'file.rs:sym' in docs/, grep -rn 'fn sym|struct sym|enum sym' over the whole crate and compare the hit's file to the cited one. angr-c7xno.25/.31/.6 (commit 8db355b0c) fixed 12 such citations in one pass.
check_line_citations.py's baseline is CONTENT-keyed (file + the citing line's text), not line-numbered, so repairing a citation leaves a dead baseline entry behind — the gate still reports '0 new', it just quietly rots. Re-run with --update-baseline after any citation-repair sweep to prune them; that is a legitimate second use of the flag alongside the 'intentionally added a citation' case CLAUDE.md documents.

emit-extract-z3-recursion-hazard: emit_extract_z3_cached (value_z3.rs) cannot be deduped against RustBV::extract_into by delegating 'inner.extract_no_ctx(high,low).to_z3_ast_cached()': that INFINITE-LOOPS. extract_no_ctx returns a RustBV::Extract node for the default case; to_z3 of an Extract node re-enters build_z3_ast_cached's BVOp::Extract arm -> emit_extract_z3_cached with the SAME (inner,high,low) -> loop. RESOLVED in angr-ph300.81: the dedup uses value_ops::drive_extract driven by the ExtractTarget trait; ExtractTarget::recurse routes back through drive_extract (NOT to_z3 of a reconstructed node), and the Z3 default terminal applies z3 .extract() to the built inner AST directly. See extract-driver-unified. The concrete fold is also shared via bv_concrete::concrete_extract_u128 (moved from bv_codec into ungated symbolic/bv_concrete.rs in angr-1yge9.14 so it builds under --no-default-features; angr-ph300.36).
endianness-test-must-touch-memory: To make a RustSimState endianness test non-vacuous you must touch MEMORY, not just registers: RegisterFile::put_reg/get_reg (arch/register_file.rs) are pure offset+size ops with no byte ordering, so a set_register/get_register round-trip passes identically under BE or LE. The little_endian flag only flows into SymbolicMemory endness (state.rs new_with_endian). Distinguishing test: map RWX page, memory_store(addr, b'\x44\x33\x22\x11') (PyO3 memory_store packs raw bytes little-endian into a u128 value=0x11223344 then stores a concrete BV using the memory endness), then memory_load(addr,1)[0] == 0x11 under BE (MSB at lowest addr) vs 0x44 under LE. A full-width memory_load(addr,4) round-trip is endness-symmetric and recovers the input bytes either way. MIPS32 arch default is_little_endian()==true (mips.rs), so little_endian=False is the only thing selecting BE — that override is what the test must make load-bearing.
export-concrete-bvv-encoding: claripy_bridge/export.rs concrete-value export: the Concrete and Constrained RustBV arms of rustbv_to_claripy_memo both go through the shared fn concrete_value_to_bvv (now in export/ast_helpers.rs), whose branch decision is the pure enum ConcreteBvvEncoding::for_width (now in export/width_decisions.rs): Int64 for w<=64, Bytes(w/8) for byte-aligned w<=128, PyIntWide otherwise. Byte-aligned width>128 (e.g. 192) MUST take PyIntWide, not Bytes: value is u128 (16 bytes) so a 24-byte PyBytes can't be built and BVV(16 bytes,192) raises ClaripyValueError 'string/size mismatch'. extract-driver-unified: Extract Rules 1-5 canonicalization (Extract/Concat/Reverse/ZeroExt/SignExt) is unified in ONE place: value_ops::drive_extract() driven by the ExtractTarget trait (angr-ph300.81). fgets-short-read-design: Native fgets short-read modeling (angr-efvao, commit 960b1eff9): variable-length read is gated behind has_option("SHORT_READS") in procedures/fgets.rs NativeFgets. When SET, mints a symbolic real_size BVS constrained 0<=real_size<=size-1 (via ule), adds Python's per-byte newline/EOF constraint If(i+1!=real_size, byte!='\n', Or(i+2==size, eof, byte=='\n')) with eof a fresh symbolic 1-bit over-approximating simfd.eof(), and RETURNS real_size (matching Python procedures/libc/fgets.py case 2 — Python's fgets returns real_size, NOT the buffer ptr, which is the actual downstream fork source). When UNSET (default), keeps the byte-identical non-forking full read, so perf gate is unaffected. KEY: the NUL terminator + data store is done as concrete-position ITE stores (byte p = ite(real_size==p, NUL, data_byte_p), final slot read_count always NUL), NOT memory_store_symbolic at a symbolic addr.

format-string-parity-defers:
Native format-string procs must DEFER to Python (return Err) on any construct where angr's Python angr/procedures/stubs/format_parser.py diverges — native must never succeed where Python errors, nor produce different bytes/arg-consumption. This cuts BOTH ways: 'native models it more faithfully than Python' is still divergence, and the faithful move is to defer, not to out-implement the reference engine.

POSITION MATTERS, not just presence: _match_spec consumes the nugget by PREFIX tests (startswith b'.*', then b'0', then b'.'), so the same field at a different offset takes a different branch. '%.*d' matches with length_spec=b'.*', but '%5.*d' / '%0.*d' route through the digit scan, leave nugget=='.*<spec>', match no all_spec entry, and fail entirely (literal '%', no vararg consumed). When mirroring a field, check WHERE it sits in the nugget, not merely that it was parsed (angr-6cp06.8).

OUTPUT side — sprintf deferred constructs (since the angr-fs8kb.44 split the shape-only defers 3/4/5/6 live in sprintf_spec.rs::parse_conversion_spec and the value-dependent ones 1/2 in sprintf_conv.rs::render_conversion): (1) %p — native emitted '0x' prefix, Python emits bare hex + sign-folds bit-63 ptrs; (2) %u/%x/%X/%o with high bit set (per modifier width) — Python's FormatSpecifier.signed is buggy so replace() sign-folds; low-bit values stay native; (3) '.N' digit precision — Python's _match_spec mis-slices the '.', drops the conversion letter, raises SimProcedureError; (4) '*' dynamic width — Python's extract_components swallows '%*' without consuming a width arg, shifting later variadic args; (5) angr-1yge9.2: '-'/'+'/' '/'#' conversion FLAGS — _match_spec has no arm for them, fails to match, emits literal '%' and does NOT consume the arg; native's flag guard in parse_conversion_spec (after the flag-parse loop, before width) returns Err when left_align||plus_sign||space_sign||hash_flag; bare '0' zero-pad + width ('%05d') is matched by both parsers and stays native; (6) angr-6cp06.8: '.*' precision NOT at nugget start ('%5.*d', '%0.*d') per POSITION MATTERS above. '%.*<spec>' at nugget start stays native but is MIRRORED not honored: FormatString.replace only reads the extra va_arg('size_t') inside its spec_type==b's' arm, so native consumes a precision vararg for %s ONLY and drops the precision for every other conversion (no zero-pad either — replace's rjust is gated on isinstance(length_spec,int) and b'.*' is not an int). %d/%i already match.

INPUT side — scanf_spec.rs::parse_scanf_format defers dynamic width, %n, unknown specifier, numeric-spec-with-unconsumed-seed, and (angr-6cp06.7) the POSIX %[...]/%[^...] SCANSET. ScanfFormatParser.basic_spec has no '[' entry and _match_spec matches a nugget only by prefix against those, so '%[a-z]' never becomes a FormatSpecifier: Python keeps the '%' as a literal one-char component and matches the bracket expression against the input stream as literal TEXT, consuming no pointer argument. Native had a full scanset impl (skip set body, mint unconstrained symbolic bytes, consume a ptr, store bytes+NUL, count a conversion) that silently disagreed on the stored buffer, the return value, and the arg bookkeeping of every conversion after it.

Do NOT 'fix' any of these by changing format_parser.py — that alters vanilla angr semantics for ALL users; parity-defer is the KISS choice. Downstream native flag-formatting code is retained but unreachable while the sprintf guard stands.
fortify-printf-chk-prototype-abi: Native fortify printf _chk family (procedures/fortify_printf.rs: NativePrintfChk/NativeSprintfChk/NativeSnprintfChk, angr-tx7ec.1) forward to base NativePrintf/NativeSprintf/NativeSnprintf, dropping glibc's injected flag/slen args (DRY, no reimplemented formatting). KEY ABI/divergence gotchas: (1) glibc _chk ABIs inject args the simplified angr decls omit — __sprintf_chk is really (char *s, int flag, size_t slen, const char *fmt, ...) but glibc.json/glibc_decls.txt declared only (S, TEMPLATE). (2) SimProcedure builds positional run() args by iterating prototype.args (sim_procedure.py:298-300), and va_arg offsets varargs past self.num_args (derived from run() signature, :160-162) — so the prototype arg count MUST equal the run() signature arg count or run() gets too few args / varargs misalign. Fixing required correcting the __sprintf_chk glibc.json proto to 4 args [S,flag,slen,TEMPLATE]+arg_names AND adding a Python __sprintf_chk(sprintf) subclass run(self,dst,flag,slen,fmt)->super().run(dst,fmt). __printf_chk/__snprintf_chk already had real Python procs+matching protos so native was a pure accelerator. fp-minmax-no-z3-fpa-min: Z3 has no fpa_min / fpa_max op (only fpa_add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/neg/abs/fma + cmp/eq/lt/leq). gate-red-triage-histogram-method:
Triaging a red ralph benchmark gate: histogram the gate's own history BEFORE bisecting.

.ralph/state/logs/iter-*-gate-stdout.txt is a ~1500-run corpus of in-gate timings for every REGRESSION_SUITE bench. Extract a bench's distribution with:

  ls -t iter-*-gate-stdout.txt | head -300 | xargs grep -h -A2 -- '--- <bench> ---' \
    | grep -oE 'Rust: +[0-9.]+s' | grep -oE '[0-9.]+'

then compare the p50/p95/max against baseline*(1+threshold). Restrict to the last ~300 logs: the full history spans code eras, so an old slow mode reads as bimodality that no longer exists (cmu_binary_bomb_partial looks 1.03/1.41-bimodal over 1580 runs, but the last 120 top out at 1.31).

This distinguishes the two causes a gate red actually has: a real regression (the whole recent distribution shifts) vs a baseline_timings.json entry captured at a quiet-host low (p50 already near the bar, a few percent of runs over it). angr-97aww was the latter — cmu_binary_bomb_partial's 1.001 baseline put 11/300 in-gate runs (3.7%) over the 15% bar. Fix is a pessimistic PINNED_RUST_TIMES entry + matching baseline_timings.json rust_time (the cow_fork_scaling/angr-x6t9o pattern), plus a test in test_timing_gate.py asserting the pin clears the recorded in-gate samples.

Corrects the too-absolute 'for non-bimodal benches, a failing gate IS a real regression - bisect it' line in benchmark-bimodal-variance-rules: load-sensitivity produces false reds on non-bimodal benches too. Bisecting is still cheap insurance (git checkout <prev> -- native/angr/src/ + tools/rebuild-rust.sh --cargo-only --keep-cargo-cache, ~2 min) and should confirm whatever the histogram says.
god-module-split-visibility-pitfall: god-module split (zel8z.*) visibility pitfall: a PRIVATE fn defined in mod.rs's main impl block is callable from sibling submodules (execution.rs, expressions.rs, etc.) because those are descendants of the module where the type is defined. Once you MOVE that fn into a new submodule, a private fn there is NOT visible to siblings -> E0624 'method is private'. Fix: widen moved private methods that sibling modules call to pub(super) (mirrors the existing pub(super) fresh_unconstrained_read). pub fn stays pub; only bare 'fn'/'fn ...' private ones need widening. Also: line-range extraction must include each struct's leading doc-comment + #[derive(...)] attrs — grabbing from 'pub struct' alone strips the derive, causing E0277 (Clone not satisfied) on the moved struct AND leaving an orphaned #[derive] that wrongly binds to the next struct (E0119 conflicting impl). Re-export moved pub structs via 'pub use submod::Struct;' to preserve crate::interpreter::* paths.
guest-value-indexing-structural-not-pani: Guest-value panic sweep of interpreter/*.rs + vex/ops/vec_*.rs (angr-qwyti.17): the raw [] indexing there is on IR-STRUCTURAL indices, NOT guest values — self.temps[*tmp as usize] (IRTemp id, bounded by tyenv), lane loops (0..count), GetI/PutI offset = base + (idx+bias)%nElems*elem_size (nElems from the VEX RegArray descriptor, not guest), elem_width/count from the op type. So the qwyti.16 arithmetic-fold panic class has NO raw-indexing analog in this layer — casts like (i as u8)/(count as u32) are structural. CAVEAT (angr-03vl4.32): 'IR-structural' does NOT mean 'validated'. IRRegArray.nElems reaches VEXInterpreter::regarray_offset via plain serde from pyvex (vex/pyvex_bridge.rs::convert_reg_array) or FFI marshalling (vex/libvex_lifter.rs::marshal_reg_array), neither of which range-checks it, so nElems==0 panicked on the %; the IR payload is itself a trust boundary and structural operands need the same InvalidIR treatment as guest ones. The ONE guest-value overflow was the arithmetic-shift sign-fill mask: (elem_mask << (elem_width - shift)) & elem_mask in vec_shift_n(Sar) + vec_shift_vec(Sar) -- since angr-5mnx3.68 both reach it through the shared per-lane core shift_lane_u128, and vec_shift_n is the merge of the former vec_shl_n/vec_shr_n/vec_sar_n, which shifts a u128 by 128 when elem_width==128 && shift==0 (panic=abort SIGABRT / release mod-128 wrap). Guarded via pub(super) VEXOps::sar_fill_mask (ops/vec_shift.rs): returns 0 when fill_bits>=128 (shift-0 fills nothing, matches reachable <128 path). Latent (NEON per-lane sar routes only <=64-bit lanes) but same class as sign_extend_to / low_bit_mask_u128 guards. Test the guard directly (VEXOps::sar_fill_mask); it is unreachable through binop dispatch.

libz3-soname-mismatch-root-cause: Two libz3 objects mapped into one process = two Z3 contexts = invalid AST handles the moment Rust touches a claripy AST. Symptom is a silent segfault, not an error. Distinguishing detail: the venv's z3-solver libz3.so has NO SONAME while the distro's is libz3.so.4, so link-time SONAME (not just RPATH) decides what dlopen resolves at runtime. Verify with: ldd target/release/librustylib.so | grep z3 -- must resolve to the venv's z3/lib/libz3.so. Two ways to get it wrong, both real: (1) the shipped .so -- native/angr/build.rs::find_z3_lib_dir shells out to whichever python3 is on PATH, so a build whose env lacks the venv silently falls back to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu (4.8.12 vs the venv's 4.13.0), and the answer is CACHED by cargo until one of the build script's rerun-if-env-changed keys (Z3_LIBRARY_PATH_OVERRIDE, PYVEX_FFI_LIB_DIR, VIRTUAL_ENV) changes -- so a later build from an activated venv reuses the wrong rpath. Force the right one with Z3_LIBRARY_PATH_OVERRIDE=$VIRTUAL_ENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages/z3/lib. (2) the cargo-test binary -- same fallback, and it is why the #[ignore]d raw-Z3-pointer tests (import_fast_path_*, sync_constraints_fp_rescued_via_z3_pointer) SIGSEGVd for a whole release cycle; their recipes now carry the override. engine.rs::install_python_z3_context (test-only) pre-flights this via mapped_libz3_objects() reading /proc/self/maps and panics with both paths named rather than segfaulting -- reach for that same procfs check whenever a new test crosses the claripy-pointer boundary.

CLAUDE.md only documents --update-baseline for the rare add-a-citation case; the prune use is the common one after a docs-fix bead (angr-9ke6b.54, commit da18f3ad1, 52->50 keys).
